input.content: Anti-pattern: removing a backward-compat fallback while an incremental migration is still in progress. In reader.address_of(row), a fallback `return row["address"]` was removed, leaving only `row["destination"]["address"]`. But migration.py:migrate_batch converts flat->nested rows in bounded batches (limit + break), meaning legacy flat rows still exist. api.list_destinations feeds every row to address_of, so un-migrated rows now raise KeyError: 'destination'. Rule: a compatibility branch is load-bearing as long as a batched/bounded migrator exists; verify 0 legacy rows (telemetry) before deleting it. Tests covered only the nested shape, so the regression passed CI.
